body:
Lords, Vassals and the Manor (lesson): King: granted fiefs to nobles; received loyalty and knights. Noble vassal: received a fief; owed loyalty and military service, and could grant land to lesser vassals. Serf: received protection, land to farm and the lord's justice; owed labor on the lord's fields, a share of crops, mill fees, and could not leave without permission. Parish priest: performed baptisms, marriages and burials; received the tithe (a tenth of produce). Guild member: received training, fair prices and a voice in town affairs; owed dues and followed guild rules.

Magna Carta, 1215 (assignment):
Sourcing 1. England's rebel barons drew up the demands; King John agreed at Runnymede in June 1215.
Sourcing 2. The barons had an army and he had lost wars and money, so he had little choice; within months the pope declared it invalid at John's request and war returned; it was reissued in 1216, 1217 and 1225.
Context 1. He had lost lands in France, demanded heavy payments for wars, and punished nobles without trial.
Context 2. Serfs were not "free men," so clause 39 did not protect most people at the time; its protections were later extended to more people.
Claim. Model: Magna Carta mainly protected barons and other free men from the king, not everyone. Clause 39 protects only a "free man" from arrest or loss of property "except by the lawful judgment of his equals or by the law of the land," and clause 12 limits the king's special payments without "common counsel," which mattered to the barons who paid them. Clause 40 promises justice to "no one" denied, which sounds broader, but in 1215 serfs mostly went to their lord's court.

The Great Mortality (assignment): Causes and spread: plague (Yersinia pestis) carried by fleas on rats and other animals, and sometimes from person to person; moved along trade routes from Central Asia; arrived by ship in Mediterranean ports in 1347 and spread across Europe by 1351. Effects: perhaps a third or more of Europe's people died; labor shortages raised wages and let peasants bargain or leave manors; lords and kings tried to fix wages (the English law of 1351); anger helped cause the Peasants' Revolt of 1381; serfdom slowly faded; Jewish communities were falsely blamed and attacked; fear and religious responses.

Which Changed More? (assessment): Either claim can earn full credit. Black Death: deaths of perhaps a third or more; wages rose; peasants left manors; Peasants' Revolt; serfdom faded. Magna Carta: limited the king by law; protected free men; its ideas grew over centuries, though in 1215 it did little directly for serfs. A strong counterclaim recognizes that Magna Carta's long-term effect was great, but its short-term effect on peasants was small (or the reverse).

Scoring tip: in the Magna Carta claim, Developing work says "it protected everyone's rights"; Proficient notices the words "free man"; Advanced explains how the meaning of the charter grew after 1215. Accept "about a third" to "half" for Black Death deaths.
